title: Oracle PAG vs FCI-Estimated PAG Comparison

oracle_pag_results.caveat: Upper bound — oracle bypasses FCI estimation error entirely. Oracle PAG is constructed directly from ground-truth FaultScenario.causal_path. This is best-case performance.
oracle_pag_results.key_failure_mode: Leaf-node R3 failure: root causes that are sink nodes in the call-graph PAG fail R3 because they have no outgoing directed edges to diverging downstream services.

fci_estimated_pag_results.reason: FCI requires real time-series telemetry from Online Boutique. Cannot produce meaningful FCI-estimated PAG from synthetic oracle metrics.

expected_direction_of_gap.claim: FCI-estimated PAG V1 <= Oracle PAG V1
expected_direction_of_gap.reasoning: FCI introduces additional error sources not present in the oracle

fci_error_sources.effect: False edges (graph too dense) or missing edges (graph too sparse)
fci_error_sources.threshold: n >= 50 samples per variable pair for reliable orientation (Phase 3 spec)

fci_error_sources.effect: Cyclic dynamics in microservices approximate faithfulness via temporal edges, but exact faithfulness is not guaranteed

fci_error_sources.source: Multiple independence tests without FDR correction
fci_error_sources.effect: At 15 variables, ~105 pairwise tests; uncorrected alpha=0.05 expects ~5 false positives
fci_error_sources.note: Phase 3 FCI uses alpha=0.05 by default; FDR not applied at the FCI level

fci_error_sources.source: Ambiguous edge marks (circle endpoints in PAG)
fci_error_sources.effect: FCI produces o-o and o-> edges where oracle has definite -> or <->; identifiability may be lower with FCI
fci_error_sources.note: Ambiguous orientations expand the NOT_IDENTIFIABLE set

expected_direction_of_gap.potential_improvement_for_leaf_nodes: FCI may orient some edges in the opposite direction relative to the call graph if temporal ordering evidence is strong. This could allow leaf-node services to satisfy R3 in some cases — but this is speculative and must not be assumed.

comparison_plan.required_setup: Online Boutique deployed on Linux with real telemetry flowing
procedure: Step 1: Run RIFT with oracle PAG on live Online Boutique scenario (NL_01)
Step 2: Run RIFT with FCI-estimated PAG on same scenario (same time window)
Step 3: Compare attribution, confidence, and identifiability state
Step 4: Repeat for at least 5 scenarios across different fault types
